questions.question: If a shopkeeper sold an article for 480, and his profit was 20% of the cost price, then the cost price was?
questions.explanation: Cost price can be found using the formula: Cost Price = (Selling Price * 100) / (100 + Profit %).

questions.question: A fruit seller bought 300 apples at Rs. 6 per apple and sold them at Rs. 9 per apple. What is his percentage profit?
questions.explanation: Profit percentage can be found using the formula: Profit Percentage = ((Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price) * 100.

questions.question: A person invested Rs. 8000 in a business for 9 months and his profit was Rs. 1400. If another person invested for 3 months, their ratio of profit will be?
questions.explanation: Profit ratio is directly proportional to the product of capital and time.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold a television at a 20% discount and still made a profit of 15%. If the marked price was Rs. 15000, then the cost price was?
questions.explanation: Cost price can be found using the formula: Cost Price = (Marked Price * (100 - Profit %)) / (100 - Discount %).

questions.question: A man bought 480 kg of potatoes at Rs. 6 per kg and sold them at Rs. 8 per kg. His profit percentage will be?
questions.explanation: Profit percentage can be found using the formula: Profit Percentage = ((Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price) * 100.

questions.question: A person can do a piece of work in 4 days, but with the help of his friend, they can do the same work in 3 days. In how many days will the friend do the work alone?

questions.question: A pipe can fill 2/3 of a tank in 1 hour. In how much time will it fill 3/4 of the tank?
questions.explanation: Since 2/3 of the tank is filled in 1 hour, 1/3 of the tank is filled in 1/2 hour.

questions.question: Two pipes P1 and P2 can fill a tank in 8 hours and 12 hours respectively. If both pipes operate simultaneously, how long will it take to fill 3/4 of the tank?
questions.explanation: Combined rate of work is 1/8 + 1/12 = 5/24 of the tank per hour.

questions.question: A tap can fill 1/3 of a tank in 2 hours. How much time will it take to fill 2/3 of the tank?
questions.explanation: Since 1/3 of the tank is filled in 2 hours, 2/3 of the tank is filled in 4 hours.

questions.question: A well with a diameter of 3 meters can be filled by two pipes. One pipe can fill 1/4 of the well in 2 hours, while the other pipe can fill 1/4 of the well in 3 hours. How long will it take to fill the well?
questions.explanation: Combined rate of work is 1/4 / 2 + 1/4 / 3 = 5/12 of the well per hour.
